site.name: Library of Pergamon

reconstruction_confidence.note: The reading rooms beside the Sanctuary of Athena Polias on the northern acropolis are among the few ancient library spaces securely identified by excavation — a colossal Athena statue was found there (now Berlin). But the arrangement of shelving and galleries is reconstructed by analogy, not recorded; any three-dimensional interior is an informed approximation.

site.evidence_summary: The library of the Attalid kings, built beside the Sanctuary of Athena Polias on the acropolis by Eumenes II (r. 197–159 BCE) as a rival to Alexandria. Reputedly some 200,000 scrolls; the city's demand for writing material is traditionally tied to the rise of parchment (charta pergamena) after a Ptolemaic papyrus embargo. It was the seat of the Pergamene school of Homeric criticism under Crates of Mallos.
site.provenance_note: Few of these works can be shown to have sat on these shelves. Galen and Crates belong here as figures OF the place; the Iliad and Heraclitus are here as the comparative material the Pergamene school actually argued from — comparanda, not catalogued holdings. The chip on each text records which is which.
